# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

53	   everything before it. Reset `lineage_watermark` /
54	   `lineage_last_refresh_at` / `lineage_last_tier` to `NULL` on both UC
55	   connections.
56	
57	**Not done (deliberately out of scope):** `trigger_bindings` / `schedules` /
58	`suite_notifications` / access-grants were not copied from prod — local
59	suites won't auto-fire on a cron or an orchestration trigger. Lineage edges
60	themselves were not copied and are not backfilled (they only populate via a
61	live refresh, which is off locally by default — same as prod).
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 2. Replication runbook (redo this from scratch)
66	
67	Run this in `~/Coding/Python/DataQ` unless noted. Requires `az` logged in
68	with Key Vault read + Container App secret read + the shared Postgres
69	server's firewall-rule permissions (deployer/`dataq-admin`-tier access).
70	
71	### 2.1 Bring up both stacks
72	
73	```bash
74	cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ
75	docker compose up -d                       # postgres/redis/openbao/mailpit/api/worker/frontend
76	
77	cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local
78	./harness_local.sh up                      # requires DataQ's stack up first (joins dataq_default)
79	```
80	
81	### 2.2 Multi-user OTP sign-in
82	
83	`.env`'s `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` **is** the allowlist — `docker-compose.yml`
84	wires it straight into `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS` verbatim
85	(`${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL?...}`, not a separate override). Comma-separate it for
86	multiple users:
87	
88	```bash
89	# .env is deliberately unwritable by the Edit tool in an AI session (secrets
90	# guard) — append with a shell redirect instead:
91	printf 'DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=you@example.com,teammate@example.com\n' >> .env
92	docker compose up -d api worker             # env is a start-time snapshot
93	```
94	
95	`WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` defaults to `dev-bypass@dataq.local,${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL}`
96	— so every signed-in address is workspace-admin by default, which is what
97	gives a freshly-provisioned local user visibility into prod's suites (they
98	belong to prod's *user rows*, not to whichever new email you sign in with;
99	workspace-admin has implicit visibility into everything, ADR 0027).
100	
101	### 2.3 Mirror OpenBao onto Key Vault (exact set, no extras)
102	
103	```bash
104	KV=dataq-app-kv-aw6laj   # re-verify with `az keyvault list` in case it's been renamed
105	source .env.app          # OPENBAO_ADDR / OPENBAO_MOUNT / OPENBAO_TOKEN
106	
107	az keyvault secret list --vault-name "$KV" --query "[?attributes.enabled].name" -o tsv | sort > /tmp/kv_names.txt
108	
109	curl -s -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "$OPENBAO_ADDR/v1/$OPENBAO_MOUNT/metadata?list=true" \
110	  | python3 -c "import json,sys; print('\n'.join(sorted(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['keys'])))" > /tmp/local_names.txt
111	
112	# purge anything local-only
113	comm -23 /tmp/local_names.txt /tmp/kv_names.txt | while read -r n; do
114	  curl -s -o /dev/null -X DELETE -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "$OPENBAO_ADDR/v1/$OPENBAO_MOUNT/metadata/$n"
115	done
116	
117	# write in every KV secret (value piped straight through, never echoed/printed)
118	while read -r n; do
119	  az keyvault secret show --vault-name "$KV" --name "$n" --query value -o tsv \
120	    | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.dumps({'data':{'value': sys.stdin.readline().rstrip(chr(10))}}))" \
121	    | curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
122	      --data-binary @- "$OPENBAO_ADDR/v1/$OPENBAO_MOUNT/data/$n"
123	done < /tmp/kv_names.txt
124	```
125	
126	**Gotcha:** this purge also deletes `dataq-local-smtp` — the bundled Mailpit
127	catcher's password, seeded locally by the one-shot `otp-mail-secret` compose
128	service. It never exists in prod Key Vault by design (prod mails via Gmail
129	SMTP under different secret names), so a strict "match KV exactly" diff
130	always removes it, and OTP sign-in then fails with
131	`otp_email_not_configured`. Fix, every time:
132	
133	```bash
134	docker compose up -d --force-recreate otp-mail-secret
135	```
136	
137	### 2.4 Wipe local seed data, pull in prod's real data
138	
139	```bash
140	cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ
141	
142	# 1. temp access to the shared prod Postgres server
143	MYIP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org)
144	az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create -g dataq-rg --server-name dataq-pg-wus3-3erlgd \
145	  --name "temp-local-sync-$(python3 -c 'import time;print(int(time.time()))')" \
146	  --start-ip-address "$MYIP" --end-ip-address "$MYIP"
147	
148	# 2. resolve prod's DATABASE_URL — it is NOT in any tfvars file (apply-time-only var);
149	#    read it straight off the live Container App secret instead:
150	export PROD_DATABASE_URL=$(az containerapp secret list -n dataq-app-api -g dataq-rg --show-values -o json \
151	  | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(next(s['value'] for s in d if s['name']=='database-url'))")
152	
153	# 3. nuke local schema, re-migrate (NO reseed — that's exactly the demo data being removed)
154	docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U dataq -d dataq -c "DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;"
155	export LOCAL_DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
156	(cd backend && DATABASE_URL="$LOCAL_DATABASE_URL" conda run -n dataq alembic upgrade head)
157	# Gotcha: `conda run -n dataq sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"` alone fails with
158	# "no password supplied" — pydantic-settings' env_file=".env.app" resolves relative to cwd,
159	# and there is no backend/.env.app (only the repo-root one). Export DATABASE_URL explicitly.
160	
161	# 4. copy users -> connections -> suites -> checks, in that FK order
162	conda run -n dataq python /path/to/sync_prod_data.py   # script below
163	
164	# 5. close the firewall rule immediately
165	RULE=$(az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule list -g dataq-rg --server-name dataq-pg-wus3-3erlgd \
166	  --query "[?starts_with(name,'temp-local-sync-')].name" -o tsv)
167	az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule delete -g dataq-rg --server-name dataq-pg-wus3-3erlgd --name "$RULE" --yes
168	```
169	
170	`sync_prod_data.py` (generic reflection-based copy, JSONB-safe, nulls
171	`asset_id` since `assets` is out of scope):
172	
173	```python
174	import os, sys
175	import psycopg2
176	import psycopg2.extras
177	
178	PROD_URL = os.environ["PROD_DATABASE_URL"].replace("postgresql+psycopg2://", "postgresql://")
179	LOCAL_URL = os.environ["LOCAL_DATABASE_URL"].replace("postgresql+psycopg2://", "postgresql://")
180	TABLES = ["users", "connections", "suites", "checks"]   # FK order
181	
182	prod = psycopg2.connect(PROD_URL); prod.set_session(readonly=True, autocommit=True)
183	local = psycopg2.connect(LOCAL_URL); local.autocommit = False
184	
185	try:
186	    with local.cursor() as lcur:
187	        for table in TABLES:
188	            with prod.cursor(cursor_factory=psycopg2.extras.RealDictCursor) as pcur:
189	                pcur.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}")
190	                rows = pcur.fetchall()
191	            if not rows:
192	                print(f"{table}: 0 rows, skipping"); continue
193	            cols = list(rows[0].keys())
194	            if "asset_id" in cols:
195	                for r in rows: r["asset_id"] = None
196	            for r in rows:
197	                for k, v in r.items():
198	                    if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
199	                        r[k] = psycopg2.extras.Json(v)
200	            col_list = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in cols)
201	            placeholders = ", ".join(f"%({c})s" for c in cols)
202	            psycopg2.extras.execute_batch(
203	                lcur, f'INSERT INTO {table} ({col_list}) VALUES ({placeholders})', rows
204	            )
205	            print(f"{table}: inserted {len(rows)} rows")
206	    local.commit(); print("COMMIT ok")
207	except Exception:
208	    local.rollback(); raise
209	finally:
210	    prod.close(); local.close()
211	```
212	
213	### 2.5 Backfill assets + fix the lineage watermark (after the copy, every time)
214	
215	The copy above bypasses `suite_service`, so `assets` stays empty until you
216	force a resolve. For every suite, `PATCH` it with its **own current**
217	`target` (fetch via `GET /suites`, resend the same `target` dict — `None`
218	means "unchanged" in this API, so you must resend it explicitly to trigger
219	resolution):
220	
221	```bash
222	curl -s -b cookies.txt -X PATCH "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/suites/$SUITE_ID" \
223	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"target\": $TARGET_JSON}"
224	```
225	
226	Then reset the UC lineage watermark so a future warehouse-lineage refresh
227	doesn't silently skip history it never actually has locally:
228	
229	```bash
230	docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U dataq -d dataq -c \
231	  "UPDATE connections SET lineage_watermark = NULL, lineage_last_refresh_at = NULL, lineage_last_tier = NULL WHERE type = 'unity_catalog';"
232	```
233	
234	(Snowflake connections don't need this — their lineage pull is a full
235	snapshot re-read each time, not incremental.)
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 3. Using this mirror for local testing
240	
241	Once §2 is done, the local stack behaves like a real, working copy of prod:
242	
243	- **Sign in** at `http://localhost:3000` (or via the OTP API directly:
244	  `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request` → read the code at
245	  `http://localhost:8025` → `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify`).
246	- **All 13 real connections and 12 real suites** are there, pointed at the
247	  actual live Snowflake/ADLS/UC/ADF/Airflow/dbt/Iceberg endpoints — a suite
248	  run genuinely queries the live warehouse, same as it would in prod. Trigger
249	  one with `POST /suites/{id}/run`, poll `GET /runs/{id}`.
250	- **Connection tests** (`POST /connections/{id}/test`) are a fast, read-only
251	  way to confirm the OpenBao mirror is intact without running a full suite.
252	- **Assets/lineage**: the asset view (`GET /assets/{id}`) works normally —
253	  scorecard, dimension coverage, linked suites. Lineage edges stay empty
254	  unless you flip `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED=true` in `.env.app` and either
255	  wait for the daily `02:37 UTC` beat task or trigger
256	  `refresh_warehouse_lineage` manually via a Celery call.
257	- **What won't work**: cron schedules and orchestration triggers, since
258	  `schedules`/`trigger_bindings` weren't copied (§1). A suite will only run
259	  when you trigger it manually.
260	- **Re-syncing later**: OpenBao is **dev-mode / in-memory** — it loses
261	  everything on `docker compose down` or a container restart. Re-run §2.3
262	  after any restart. The DB copy in §2.4 is durable (real Postgres volume)
263	  until you next reset it.
264	
265	---
266	
267	## 4. Utilizing the local Airflow + MinIO stack
268	
269	**As of this session, they are up but genuinely unused** — none of the 13
270	prod-mirrored connections point at them (they all point at the real Azure
271	endpoints, matching prod). MinIO's `landing` bucket and the Airflow scheduler
272	still hold state from an **older** session (mockdata seeded 2026-07-27; DAG
273	runs `flow_a_snowflake_load` / `flow_a_uc_reference` / `flow_b_medallion`
274	last shown `failed` from that same old run) — nothing from the 2026-08-03
275	session touched them.
276	
277	To actually exercise them, two independent things need to happen:
278	
279	**A. Re-seed / re-run the harness itself** (tests the ETL flow in isolation,
280	nothing to do with DataQ yet):
281	
282	```bash
283	cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local
284	./harness_local.sh seed          # backfill mockdata -> MinIO
285	./harness_local.sh run --dags    # unpause + REST-trigger the cron DAGs
286	./harness_local.sh status        # container + DAG state
287	```
288	
289	Airflow UI: `http://localhost:8080` (admin / see `local/.env`). MinIO
290	console: `http://localhost:9001`.
291	
292	**B. Point a DataQ connection at them** (this is what actually puts them in
293	DataQ's monitoring path — see the harness README's "Point DataQ at it"
294	section for the full detail, summarized here):
295	
296	- **MinIO as an `s3` connection** (DataQ #1063, ordinary `s3` connection
297	  type, no special local mode): `bucket=landing`, `region=us-east-1`,
298	  `endpoint_url=http://minio:9000`, access key/secret =
299	  `MINIO_ROOT_USER`/`MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` (from `local/.env`). Leave
300	  addressing style `auto` — it resolves to **path** style automatically
301	  because an endpoint is set (MinIO only serves the bucket in the path).
302	- **Local Airflow as an `airflow` connection**: `base_url=http://airflow-webserver:8080`,
303	  basic auth, user `admin`, password from `local/.env`.
304	
305	Either create these as **new, additional** local-only connections/suites (so
306	you don't disturb the prod-mirrored ones), or temporarily repoint one of the
307	mirrored flat-file/orchestration connections at the local endpoints if you
308	specifically want to compare local vs. prod behavior on the same suite
309	definition.
310	
311	This combination (§4A + §4B) was **validated end-to-end once already**, on
312	2026-07-27, before this session (see DataQ's `docs/ops-log.md`): 4 DAGs
313	parsed clean, 24 datasets seeded, DataQ connection test green, flat-file
314	suite 4/4 (643 rows, arrival-time freshness read off MinIO's
315	`LastModified`), `flow_a_snowflake_load` succeeded into live Snowflake, and
316	DataQ ingested the local DAG runs into `pipeline_runs`. That state is what's
317	currently sitting stale in the containers — re-running §4A brings it current
318	again; §4B (the DataQ-side connection) was not re-created this session and
319	would need to be added again if you want DataQ itself watching the local
320	harness rather than just the harness running standalone.
321	
322	---
323	
324	## 5. Teardown
325	
326	```bash
327	# local harness
328	cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local
329	./harness_local.sh down            # add --volumes to also drop the metadata DB + MinIO data
330	
331	# DataQ stack
332	cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ
333	docker compose down                 # add -v to also drop Postgres/OpenBao data
334	```
335	
336	Nothing here touches Azure/prod — every prod-facing action in §2 is either
337	read-only (`az keyvault secret show`, the prod `SELECT`s) or explicitly
338	scoped and reverted (the firewall rule).

# Local DataQ ⟷ prod mirror — session summary + runbook

**Session: 2026-08-03.** DataQ's local dev stack was converted into a live
mirror of prod (real secrets, real connections/suites, real datasource
traffic) and the local harness stack (this repo's `local/`) was brought up
alongside it. This doc is the replication runbook for redoing that, plus
guidance on using the mirror day-to-day and on actually exercising the local
Airflow/MinIO stack (which, as of this session, sits up but **unused** — see
§4).

Companion: DataQ's own memory note
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/memory/project_local_prod_mirror_setup.md`
carries the same gotchas for AI-assistant sessions; this file is the
human-readable, repo-anchored version.

---

## 1. What was done this session

1. **Brought up DataQ's own compose stack** (`docker compose up -d` in
   `~/Coding/Python/DataQ`) — postgres/redis/openbao/mailpit/api/worker/frontend,
   all default services.
2. **Brought up this repo's local harness** (`local/harness_local.sh up`) —
   Airflow (Postgres+Redis+CeleryExecutor) + MinIO, joined onto DataQ's
   compose network.
3. **Configured multi-user email-OTP sign-in** by setting `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL`
   in DataQ's root `.env` — see the gotcha in §2.2, this is the ONE switch,
   not a separately-settable allowlist.
4. **Mirrored local OpenBao onto Azure Key Vault exactly** — purged 143
   unrelated stale secrets from a prior local session, wrote in the 25 real
   `dataq-app-kv-aw6laj` secrets by name (values piped directly between `az`
   and OpenBao's HTTP API, never printed or written to disk), verified the
   name sets are now identical.
5. **Replaced local DB seed/demo data with prod's real `users` /
   `connections` / `suites` / `checks`** — nuked the local schema, re-ran
   migrations, opened a **temporary** Postgres firewall rule, copied the four
   tables straight from prod via `psycopg2`, closed the firewall rule
   immediately after. 13 connections, 12 suites, 30 checks, 8 users.
6. **Verified functionality**: OTP sign-in end-to-end (Mailpit), suite runs
   across Snowflake / ADLS flat-file / Unity Catalog (all green, including a
   deliberately-seeded prod failure behaving as expected) / Iceberg (failed —
   see §2.5, expected given the closed firewall rule).
7. **Backfilled asset resolution** — the raw DB copy bypassed the service
   layer that normally creates an `assets` row on suite save, so `GET
   /assets` was empty. Fixed by re-`PATCH`ing each suite with its own
   existing `target`, which forces `resolve_and_upsert_asset` without
   changing anything else. 10 assets now exist, correctly deduplicated.
8. **Reset a latent lineage-sync landmine** — the copied Unity Catalog
   connections carried prod's *incremental* lineage watermark
   (`2026-07-27`) into a local DB whose `lineage_edges` table was never
   copied. Left alone, a future local warehouse-lineage refresh would have
   silently started from that stale cursor and permanently skipped
   everything before it. Reset `lineage_watermark` /
   `lineage_last_refresh_at` / `lineage_last_tier` to `NULL` on both UC
   connections.

**Not done (deliberately out of scope):** `trigger_bindings` / `schedules` /
`suite_notifications` / access-grants were not copied from prod — local
suites won't auto-fire on a cron or an orchestration trigger. Lineage edges
themselves were not copied and are not backfilled (they only populate via a
live refresh, which is off locally by default — same as prod).

---

## 2. Replication runbook (redo this from scratch)

with Key Vault read + Container App secret read + the shared Postgres
server's firewall-rule permissions (deployer/`dataq-admin`-tier access).

cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local

`sync_prod_data.py` (generic reflection-based copy, JSONB-safe, nulls

```python
import os, sys
import psycopg2
import psycopg2.extras

PROD_URL = os.environ["PROD_DATABASE_URL"].replace("postgresql+psycopg2://", "postgresql://")

TABLES = ["users", "connections", "suites", "checks"]   # FK order

prod = psycopg2.connect(PROD_URL); prod.set_session(readonly=True, autocommit=True)
local = psycopg2.connect(LOCAL_URL); local.autocommit = False

try:
    with local.cursor() as lcur:
        for table in TABLES:
            with prod.cursor(cursor_factory=psycopg2.extras.RealDictCursor) as pcur:
                pcur.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}")
                rows = pcur.fetchall()
            if not rows:
                print(f"{table}: 0 rows, skipping"); continue
            cols = list(rows[0].keys())
            if "asset_id" in cols:
                for r in rows: r["asset_id"] = None
            for r in rows:
                for k, v in r.items():
                    if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                        r[k] = psycopg2.extras.Json(v)
            col_list = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in cols)
            placeholders = ", ".join(f"%({c})s" for c in cols)
            psycopg2.extras.execute_batch(
                lcur, f'INSERT INTO {table} ({col_list}) VALUES ({placeholders})', rows
            )
            print(f"{table}: inserted {len(rows)} rows")
    local.commit(); print("COMMIT ok")
except Exception:
    local.rollback(); raise
finally:
    prod.close(); local.close()
```

### 2.5 Backfill assets + fix the lineage watermark (after the copy, every time)

The copy above bypasses `suite_service`, so `assets` stays empty until you
force a resolve. For every suite, `PATCH` it with its **own current**
`target` (fetch via `GET /suites`, resend the same `target` dict — `None`
means "unchanged" in this API, so you must resend it explicitly to trigger
resolution):

```bash
curl -s -b cookies.txt -X PATCH "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/suites/$SUITE_ID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"target\": $TARGET_JSON}"
```

Then reset the UC lineage watermark so a future warehouse-lineage refresh
doesn't silently skip history it never actually has locally:

```bash
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U dataq -d dataq -c \
  "UPDATE connections SET lineage_watermark = NULL, lineage_last_refresh_at = NULL, lineage_last_tier = NULL WHERE type = 'unity_catalog';"
```

(Snowflake connections don't need this — their lineage pull is a full
snapshot re-read each time, not incremental.)

---

## 3. Using this mirror for local testing

Once §2 is done, the local stack behaves like a real, working copy of prod:

- **Sign in** at `http://localhost:3000` (or via the OTP API directly:
  `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request` → read the code at
  `http://localhost:8025` → `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify`).
- **All 13 real connections and 12 real suites** are there, pointed at the
  actual live Snowflake/ADLS/UC/ADF/Airflow/dbt/Iceberg endpoints — a suite
  run genuinely queries the live warehouse, same as it would in prod. Trigger
  one with `POST /suites/{id}/run`, poll `GET /runs/{id}`.
- **Connection tests** (`POST /connections/{id}/test`) are a fast, read-only
  way to confirm the OpenBao mirror is intact without running a full suite.
- **Assets/lineage**: the asset view (`GET /assets/{id}`) works normally —
  scorecard, dimension coverage, linked suites. Lineage edges stay empty
  unless you flip `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED=true` in `.env.app` and either
  wait for the daily `02:37 UTC` beat task or trigger
  `refresh_warehouse_lineage` manually via a Celery call.
- **What won't work**: cron schedules and orchestration triggers, since
  `schedules`/`trigger_bindings` weren't copied (§1). A suite will only run
  when you trigger it manually.
- **Re-syncing later**: OpenBao is **dev-mode / in-memory** — it loses
  everything on `docker compose down` or a container restart. Re-run §2.3
  after any restart. The DB copy in §2.4 is durable (real Postgres volume)
  until you next reset it.

---

## 4. Utilizing the local Airflow + MinIO stack

**As of this session, they are up but genuinely unused** — none of the 13
prod-mirrored connections point at them (they all point at the real Azure
endpoints, matching prod). MinIO's `landing` bucket and the Airflow scheduler
still hold state from an **older** session (mockdata seeded 2026-07-27; DAG
runs `flow_a_snowflake_load` / `flow_a_uc_reference` / `flow_b_medallion`
last shown `failed` from that same old run) — nothing from the 2026-08-03
session touched them.

To actually exercise them, two independent things need to happen:

**A. Re-seed / re-run the harness itself** (tests the ETL flow in isolation,
nothing to do with DataQ yet):

```bash
cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local
./harness_local.sh seed          # backfill mockdata -> MinIO
./harness_local.sh run --dags    # unpause + REST-trigger the cron DAGs
./harness_local.sh status        # container + DAG state
```

Airflow UI: `http://localhost:8080` (admin / see `local/.env`). MinIO
console: `http://localhost:9001`.

**B. Point a DataQ connection at them** (this is what actually puts them in
DataQ's monitoring path — see the harness README's "Point DataQ at it"
section for the full detail, summarized here):

- **MinIO as an `s3` connection** (DataQ #1063, ordinary `s3` connection
  type, no special local mode): `bucket=landing`, `region=us-east-1`,
  `endpoint_url=http://minio:9000`, access key/secret =
  `MINIO_ROOT_USER`/`MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` (from `local/.env`). Leave
  addressing style `auto` — it resolves to **path** style automatically
  because an endpoint is set (MinIO only serves the bucket in the path).
- **Local Airflow as an `airflow` connection**: `base_url=http://airflow-webserver:8080`,
  basic auth, user `admin`, password from `local/.env`.

Either create these as **new, additional** local-only connections/suites (so
you don't disturb the prod-mirrored ones), or temporarily repoint one of the
mirrored flat-file/orchestration connections at the local endpoints if you
specifically want to compare local vs. prod behavior on the same suite
definition.

This combination (§4A + §4B) was **validated end-to-end once already**, on
2026-07-27, before this session (see DataQ's `docs/ops-log.md`): 4 DAGs
parsed clean, 24 datasets seeded, DataQ connection test green, flat-file
suite 4/4 (643 rows, arrival-time freshness read off MinIO's
`LastModified`), `flow_a_snowflake_load` succeeded into live Snowflake, and
DataQ ingested the local DAG runs into `pipeline_runs`. That state is what's
currently sitting stale in the containers — re-running §4A brings it current
again; §4B (the DataQ-side connection) was not re-created this session and
would need to be added again if you want DataQ itself watching the local
harness rather than just the harness running standalone.

---

## 5. Teardown

```bash
# local harness
cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local
./harness_local.sh down            # add --volumes to also drop the metadata DB + MinIO data

# DataQ stack
cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ
docker compose down                 # add -v to also drop Postgres/OpenBao data
```

Nothing here touches Azure/prod — every prod-facing action in §2 is either
read-only (`az keyvault secret show`, the prod `SELECT`s) or explicitly
scoped and reverted (the firewall rule).

`ROYARIJIT04`, role `DATAQ_READER`, `DATAQ_DB`/`RETAIL`/`DATAQ_WH`) and differ *only* in which
secret they read. **On any credential rotation, write ALL `conn-*` secrets that share it, then
prove it with `POST /connections/{id}/test` per connection** — the connections list will look
identical whether they are alive or dead.

the `SecretStore` reads Key Vault **at runtime**, so the next test/run picks it up

/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/feature-matrix.md
# Feature matrix

One-page reference: what runs where. For the readable tour of everything DataQ offers see
[Features](features.md); for the concepts behind the columns see [Concepts](concepts.md) and
[Datasources & checks](datasources-checks.md).

## Check kinds × datasources

| Check kind | Snowflake | Unity Catalog | ADLS Gen2 (files) | S3 (files)ˢ | Iceberg |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| GX expectations (column / table shape) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Custom SQL (rows returned = failures) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Freshness monitor (hours since latest timestamp) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Freshness from **file arrival time** (no column — catches "no new file") | — | — | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Volume monitor (row count in range) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Anomaly monitor (z-score vs a learned baseline)ᵃ | ✅ | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Schema-drift monitor (column add/drop/type-change vs a stored baseline)ᵇ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Comparison / reconciliation (diff vs a baseline connection) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Column profiler (nulls, distinct, min/max, top values) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| DQ dimension on checks + asset scorecard (coverage + score) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Dry-run preview | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

ᵃ **Live-verified 2026-08-01.** The anomaly monitor (#593, PRs #1117/#1119 — backend
engine plus its check-editor authoring UI) learns a rolling mean/stddev of the
target's own row count or freshness age (optionally per weekday) and bands each
run's z-score through the usual warn/fail/critical thresholds; below its
`min_points` of history it reports `skip`, never a fabricated pass. Both target
metrics were run against both live warehouses via the real `measure_metric` path
(the standing rule after #953 shipped a ✅ that had never once worked — only an
**executed** run against a live datasource earns the tick): Snowflake
`RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER` row_count=34680.0 + freshness `ORDER_TS`=132.28h; Unity
Catalog `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment` row_count=180.0 + freshness
`scored_at`=132.48h. The dashes are a real restriction, not an omission: the
anomaly executor takes its own measurement over a live SQL connection, while
Iceberg and flat files compute their monitor scalars natively inside their
runners, which stateful kinds never reach.

ᵇ **Schema drift** (ADR 0012, [#592](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/592))
diffs a live column-name/type snapshot against a stored baseline and flags
add/drop/type-change. Unlike custom SQL it never goes through a `CheckRunner`/GX at
all, so it isn't gated to SQL datasources: introspection is per-datasource —
`information_schema` for Snowflake/Unity Catalog, the Parquet footer or a bounded
CSV header sample for ADLS/S3 flat files, and the loaded table's own metadata for
Iceberg (no data scan on any of them except the CSV sample). Re-baseline explicitly
once a drift is expected and reviewed.

ˢ **S3 means AWS S3 *and* any S3-compatible store** — MinIO, Ceph/RadosGW, Cloudflare R2,
Wasabi, Backblaze B2, SeaweedFS or an on-prem gateway. Set the connection's optional
endpoint URL (#1063); every row in this column applies identically either way. See
[Datasources & checks](datasources-checks.md#s3-compatible-object-stores).

Custom SQL runs a SQL query, so it's **SQL-datasource only** (Snowflake, Unity Catalog;
there is no flat-file support, and no issue currently tracks adding it — flat files get freshness/volume monitors instead (see the rows above);
Iceberg is not SQL-queryable — reads go through `pyiceberg` scans, not a query engine).
**Comparison checks** (ADR [0015](adr/0015-two-connection-comparison-check-model.md), #791–#795)
diff the suite's dataset (the **target under test**) against a baseline on any other
datasource connection — cross-type and cross-env both supported — joined on key columns,
producing matched / mismatched / additional-per-side buckets with a mismatch-% metric,
capped fail-fast reads (`COMPARISON_MAX_ROWS`), redacted samples, and an on-demand
CSV/XLSX report download (derived, never stored). Either SQL side may use a read-only
query projection.

The freshness/volume monitors run on **every datasource** — the SQL datasources, Apache
Iceberg (computed natively via `pyiceberg` scans, not SQL; ADR 0012/0030), and ADLS Gen2 /
S3 flat files (over the resolved batch; #520). On a flat file, a freshness monitor with **no
timestamp column** measures the object's arrival time instead — catching a producer that
stopped sending files, which a timestamp inside the data cannot see. Flat-file suites target a file or a batch pattern (e.g.
`orders_*.csv`) in CSV or Parquet; Iceberg suites target a `namespace.table`. Dry-run
preview works on every datasource with a runner — Snowflake, Unity Catalog, flat files,
and Iceberg ([#532](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/532)).

## Assets & lineage × datasources

Every datasource gets a first-class **asset** (identity = the OpenLineage dataset naming
spec, ADR 0034); lineage edges are **observed, never inferred**, and can arrive through
five mechanisms:

1. **Run-stamping** — every suite run (and suite save) resolves its target to an asset row
   and stamps `last_seen`. Works on all datasources; unreferenced stale rows are retired by
   the daily orphan sweep.
2. **dbt `manifest.json`** — table-level model lineage cached into `lineage_edges` on every
   successful dbt build ([details](orchestration.md#lineage-from-manifestjson-adr-0034)).

# Feature matrix

One-page reference: what runs where. For the readable tour of everything DataQ offers see
[Features](features.md); for the concepts behind the columns see [Concepts](concepts.md) and
[Datasources & checks](datasources-checks.md).

## Check kinds × datasources

| Check kind | Snowflake | Unity Catalog | ADLS Gen2 (files) | S3 (files)ˢ | Iceberg |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| GX expectations (column / table shape) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Custom SQL (rows returned = failures) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Freshness monitor (hours since latest timestamp) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Freshness from **file arrival time** (no column — catches "no new file") | — | — | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Volume monitor (row count in range) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Anomaly monitor (z-score vs a learned baseline)ᵃ | ✅ | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Schema-drift monitor (column add/drop/type-change vs a stored baseline)ᵇ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Comparison / reconciliation (diff vs a baseline connection) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Column profiler (nulls, distinct, min/max, top values) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| DQ dimension on checks + asset scorecard (coverage + score) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Dry-run preview | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

ᵃ **Live-verified 2026-08-01.** The anomaly monitor (#593, PRs #1117/#1119 — backend
engine plus its check-editor authoring UI) learns a rolling mean/stddev of the
target's own row count or freshness age (optionally per weekday) and bands each
run's z-score through the usual warn/fail/critical thresholds; below its
`min_points` of history it reports `skip`, never a fabricated pass. Both target
metrics were run against both live warehouses via the real `measure_metric` path
(the standing rule after #953 shipped a ✅ that had never once worked — only an
**executed** run against a live datasource earns the tick): Snowflake
`RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER` row_count=34680.0 + freshness `ORDER_TS`=132.28h; Unity
Catalog `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment` row_count=180.0 + freshness
`scored_at`=132.48h. The dashes are a real restriction, not an omission: the
anomaly executor takes its own measurement over a live SQL connection, while
Iceberg and flat files compute their monitor scalars natively inside their
runners, which stateful kinds never reach.

ᵇ **Schema drift** (ADR 0012, [#592](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/592))
diffs a live column-name/type snapshot against a stored baseline and flags
add/drop/type-change. Unlike custom SQL it never goes through a `CheckRunner`/GX at
all, so it isn't gated to SQL datasources: introspection is per-datasource —
`information_schema` for Snowflake/Unity Catalog, the Parquet footer or a bounded
CSV header sample for ADLS/S3 flat files, and the loaded table's own metadata for
Iceberg (no data scan on any of them except the CSV sample). Re-baseline explicitly
once a drift is expected and reviewed.

ˢ **S3 means AWS S3 *and* any S3-compatible store** — MinIO, Ceph/RadosGW, Cloudflare R2,
Wasabi, Backblaze B2, SeaweedFS or an on-prem gateway. Set the connection's optional
endpoint URL (#1063); every row in this column applies identically either way. See
[Datasources & checks](datasources-checks.md#s3-compatible-object-stores).

Custom SQL runs a SQL query, so it's **SQL-datasource only** (Snowflake, Unity Catalog;
there is no flat-file support, and no issue currently tracks adding it — flat files get freshness/volume monitors instead (see the rows above);
Iceberg is not SQL-queryable — reads go through `pyiceberg` scans, not a query engine).
**Comparison checks** (ADR [0015](adr/0015-two-connection-comparison-check-model.md), #791–#795)
diff the suite's dataset (the **target under test**) against a baseline on any other
datasource connection — cross-type and cross-env both supported — joined on key columns,
producing matched / mismatched / additional-per-side buckets with a mismatch-% metric,
capped fail-fast reads (`COMPARISON_MAX_ROWS`), redacted samples, and an on-demand
CSV/XLSX report download (derived, never stored). Either SQL side may use a read-only
query projection.

The freshness/volume monitors run on **every datasource** — the SQL datasources, Apache
Iceberg (computed natively via `pyiceberg` scans, not SQL; ADR 0012/0030), and ADLS Gen2 /
S3 flat files (over the resolved batch; #520). On a flat file, a freshness monitor with **no
timestamp column** measures the object's arrival time instead — catching a producer that
stopped sending files, which a timestamp inside the data cannot see. Flat-file suites target a file or a batch pattern (e.g.
`orders_*.csv`) in CSV or Parquet; Iceberg suites target a `namespace.table`. Dry-run
preview works on every datasource with a runner — Snowflake, Unity Catalog, flat files,
and Iceberg ([#532](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/532)).

spec, ADR 0034); lineage edges are **observed, never inferred**, and can arrive through

1. **Run-stamping** — every suite run (and suite save) resolves its target to an asset row

   [details](orchestration.md#lineage-from-a-catalog-the-lineageprovider-seam-adr-0034-762)).
5. **Warehouse-native pull** (#858) — the `WarehouseLineageProvider` seam reads the
   warehouse's OWN lineage views straight into `lineage_edges` with `source='snowflake'` /
   `'unity_catalog'`: Snowflake `OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES` (all editions) → `ACCESS_HISTORY` /
   `GET_LINEAGE` (Enterprise); Unity Catalog `system.access.table_lineage`. First-hand, no
   dbt hop. Daily beat, **dark by default** (`WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED` — the views need a
   grant); the tier that answered and any degraded/failing state surface on the asset's
   lineage graph so a view-level-only or stale graph never reads as a confident complete
   one ([details](orchestration.md#lineage-from-the-warehouse-the-warehouselineageprovider-seam-858)).
   **Column grain (#901):** where the warehouse offers it (UC

   workspace member (ADR 0037 — column names are schema metadata, i.e. identity).

**Prod** (API inventory as `dataq-admin` via the KV admin PAT, which still works despite the 08-04 expiry note):
- **13 connections** — all healthy except the two Airflow connections (~2,000 consecutive poll failures each — expected, the harness Airflow ACA is **Stopped**; not a credential issue). Creds: ADLS SAS good to 2027, UC PATs, Snowflake fine.
- **12 suites / 30 checks** (24 expectation, 3 freshness, 1 volume — no schema-drift/anomaly/comparison anywhere today), 8 suites shared, 6 owners (5 demo users + dataq-admin).

**Local**: the whole stack (DataQ compose + local Airflow/MinIO harness) is **down** — everything exited shortly before I checked. The Postgres volume survives (the 08-03 prod mirror should be intact), but **OpenBao is in-memory dev mode, so all mirrored secrets are gone** and must be re-mirrored from Key Vault before anything can run locally.

## Plan

**Phase 0 — Local bring-up** (sonnet agent): `docker compose up -d` + `harness_local.sh up`; re-mirror KV→OpenBao per the runbook §2.3 (inline-only secret handling); re-seed `dataq-local-smtp` (`otp-mail-secret`); verify OTP sign-in + a couple of `POST /connections/{id}/test`. Re-seed MinIO mockdata (`harness_local.sh seed`) so flat-file targets have fresh data.

**Phase 1 — Wipe** (haiku agent, serialized after Phase 0):
- Prod: delete 5 schedules → 1 dbt trigger binding → all 12 suites (cascade removes the 30 checks + shares). **Connections are kept** — all 13 are reused. This also removes the deliberately-failing "seeded breach" check and the dbt-lineage demo suite; noting that explicitly since both were intentional fixtures.
- Local: delete the 12 mirrored suites (no schedules/bindings exist locally — they were never copied).

**Phase 2 — Author new suites through the UI (Playwright, serialized one env at a time)** — no API/DB inserts, per your instruction. Proposed matrix (~30 checks total per environment):

| Suite | Connection (prod / local) | Target | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Snowflake — Orders (all paths) | Snowflake — Retail (both envs, live SF) | RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER | not-null, unique, in-set, custom SQL, freshness(ORDER_TS), volume, anomaly(row_count), schema drift, comparison (baseline: Snowflake — Orders conn) — **9 checks, every kind SF supports** |
| Unity Catalog — Feedback (all paths) | UC — dataq_retail (both envs, live UC) | gold.feedback_sentiment | same 9 shapes — every kind UC supports |
| Iceberg — Purchase Orders | prod: harness-iceberg (ADLS) / local: see Q2 | retail.purchase_orders | not-null, between, freshness, volume, schema drift (+comparison) — all Iceberg supports (no SQL/anomaly by design) |
| Flat file — Logistics | prod: ADLS landing / local: **new MinIO `s3` connection** | tracking_events batch pattern | not-null, in-set, column freshness, **arrival-time freshness**, volume, schema drift — all flat-file supports |

Local additionally needs two new connections created via UI: MinIO `s3` (`endpoint_url=http://minio:9000`, bucket `landing`) and local Airflow (`http://airflow-webserver:8080`).

**Phase 3 — Airflow trigger bindings**: prod → Azure harness Airflow connection; local → the new local Airflow connection. Natural bindings: Snowflake suite → `flow_a_snowflake_load`, UC suite → `flow_b_medallion`. Caveat: **no Airflow DAG feeds Iceberg or the ADLS landing zone in prod** (those are ACA jobs), so those two either stay manual/scheduled or get a proxy binding to `flow_b_medallion`. Also note prod bindings only ever fire during a harness window — the Azure Airflow is stopped by default.

1	"""Flow D — Apache Iceberg writer (no orchestrator).
2	
3	Each ``iceberg-tick`` appends a referentially-consistent batch of purchase-order
4	rows to the Iceberg table ``retail.purchase_orders`` via a pyiceberg **SqlCatalog**
5	(Postgres-backed metadata) with an **ADLS (abfss) warehouse** read through
6	fsspec/adlfs. DataQ reads the same table **natively** (its ``iceberg`` connection,
7	ADR 0030) on its own DataQ schedule — there is **no orchestrator and no
8	trigger-binding** (the Flow-C precedent: nothing "loads" this for DataQ to react to).
9	
10	Self-contained by design — unlike the ``tick`` feeds this needs **no persisted
11	state file**. Each tick simply appends another snapshot (idempotent-safe: re-running
12	just adds another batch). ``po_id`` is namespaced by the tick's wall-clock so two
13	ticks never collide (which would forge an *accidental* duplicate and muddy the one
14	*deliberate* duplicate we seed). Supplier / product ids come from the same seeded
15	pools idiom (``rng.id_pool``) the rest of the harness uses, so they read as the same
16	id space as Flow A's ``suppliers`` / ``products``.
17	
18	Seeded DQ issues per tick (mirrors ``dq_issues.py`` rates/style) give DataQ's checks
19	something real to bite on: ~1-2% negative ``order_qty`` (fails a ``order_qty >= 0``
20	range check), ~1% null ``supplier_id`` (fails ``not_null supplier_id``), and a rare
21	duplicate ``(po_id, po_line)`` (fails a uniqueness check).
22	
23	The pyiceberg / pyarrow imports are module-local to the functions that need a live
24	catalog so ``python -m mockdata --help`` (and the other subcommands) don't pay for
25	them; ``iceberg-tick`` is the only path that requires the Iceberg deps.
26	"""
27	
28	from __future__ import annotations
29	
30	import datetime as dt
31	import os
32	from typing import Any
33	
34	from .rng import Rng
35	
36	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
37	# Table coordinates + generation shape.
38	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
39	
40	NAMESPACE = "retail"
41	TABLE = "purchase_orders"
42	IDENTIFIER = f"{NAMESPACE}.{TABLE}"
43	
44	# Referential pools (same id shapes as Flow A: SUP-#### width 4, SKU-###### width 6).
45	N_SUPPLIERS = 30
46	N_PRODUCTS = 200
47	
48	# Batch sizing + issue rates (mirror dq_issues.py: low single-digit %).
49	DEFAULT_ROWS_MIN = 200
50	DEFAULT_ROWS_MAX = 500
51	NEG_QTY_RATE = 0.015  # ~1.5% negative order_qty
52	NULL_SUPPLIER_RATE = 0.01  # ~1% null supplier_id
53	DUP_RATE = 0.005  # ~0.5% duplicated (po_id, po_line) rows
54	
55	PO_STATUSES = ["open", "partial", "received", "cancelled"]
56	CURRENCIES = ["USD", "EUR", "GBP", "CAD", "JPY"]
57	
58	
59	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
60	# Catalog wiring.
61	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
62	
63	
64	def catalog_properties_from_env() -> dict[str, str]:
65	    """Compose ``load_catalog`` / ``SqlCatalog`` properties from the Job's env.
66	
67	    ``ICEBERG_CATALOG_URI`` (the Postgres SQLAlchemy DSN, secret) + ``ICEBERG_WAREHOUSE``
68	    (the ``abfss://iceberg@<acct>.dfs.core.windows.net/warehouse`` root) + the ADLS
69	    account name/key for the fsspec (adlfs) FileIO. Mirrors the DataQ ``iceberg``
70	    connection's own catalog properties (``IcebergConfig.catalog_properties``) so both
71	    sides read the same table the same way.
72	    """
73	    uri = os.environ["ICEBERG_CATALOG_URI"]
74	    warehouse = os.environ["ICEBERG_WAREHOUSE"]
75	    props: dict[str, str] = {
76	        "uri": uri,
77	        "warehouse": warehouse,
78	        # Native (no query engine) object-store IO through fsspec/adlfs.
79	        "py-io-impl": "pyiceberg.io.fsspec.FsspecFileIO",
80	    }
81	    account = os.environ.get("AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME")
82	    key = os.environ.get("AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_KEY")
83	    if account:
84	        props["adls.account-name"] = account
85	    if key:
86	        props["adls.account-key"] = key
87	    return props
88	
89	
90	def build_catalog(
91	    name: str = "harness", *, properties: dict[str, str] | None = None
92	) -> Any:
93	    """Load a pyiceberg ``SqlCatalog`` (env-driven by default).
94	
95	    ``properties`` overrides the env composition — the local sqlite smoke passes a
96	    ``sqlite://`` uri + a ``file://`` warehouse so the writer's real code paths run
97	    with no Azure. pyiceberg is imported here so the CLI stays import-cheap.
98	    """
99	    from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog
100	
101	    props = properties if properties is not None else catalog_properties_from_env()
102	    return SqlCatalog(name, **props)
103	
104	
105	def _iceberg_schema() -> Any:
106	    """The ``retail.purchase_orders`` Iceberg schema (v2).
107	
108	    ``po_id`` / ``po_line`` / ``load_ts`` are required (the batch always populates
109	    them); everything else is **optional** so the seeded null ``supplier_id`` lands
110	    instead of being rejected at write time. ``unit_cost`` is a ``double`` — it
111	    round-trips through pyarrow cleanly, avoiding decimal128 scale/precision friction
112	    on ``table.append`` (the design's allowed choice).
113	    """
114	    from pyiceberg.schema import Schema
115	    from pyiceberg.types import (
116	        DateType,
117	        DoubleType,
118	        IntegerType,
119	        NestedField,
120	        StringType,
121	        TimestamptzType,
122	    )
123	
124	    return Schema(
125	        NestedField(1, "po_id", StringType(), required=True),
126	        NestedField(2, "po_line", IntegerType(), required=True),
127	        NestedField(3, "supplier_id", StringType(), required=False),
128	        NestedField(4, "product_id", StringType(), required=False),
129	        NestedField(5, "order_qty", IntegerType(), required=False),
130	        NestedField(6, "unit_cost", DoubleType(), required=False),
131	        NestedField(7, "currency", StringType(), required=False),
132	        NestedField(8, "status", StringType(), required=False),
133	        NestedField(9, "ordered_at", TimestamptzType(), required=False),
134	        NestedField(10, "expected_delivery", DateType(), required=False),
135	        NestedField(11, "load_ts", TimestamptzType(), required=True),
136	    )
137	
138	
139	def _arrow_schema() -> Any:
140	    """pyarrow schema matching ``_iceberg_schema`` (nullability + widths aligned).
141	
142	    IntegerType → int32; TimestamptzType → ``timestamp('us', tz='UTC')`` (pyiceberg's
143	    required microsecond precision); DateType → date32. Nullable flags mirror the
144	    Iceberg ``required`` flags so ``table.append`` accepts the frame."""
145	    import pyarrow as pa
146	
147	    return pa.schema(
148	        [
149	            pa.field("po_id", pa.string(), nullable=False),
150	            pa.field("po_line", pa.int32(), nullable=False),
151	            pa.field("supplier_id", pa.string(), nullable=True),
152	            pa.field("product_id", pa.string(), nullable=True),
153	            pa.field("order_qty", pa.int32(), nullable=True),
154	            pa.field("unit_cost", pa.float64(), nullable=True),
155	            pa.field("currency", pa.string(), nullable=True),
156	            pa.field("status", pa.string(), nullable=True),
157	            pa.field("ordered_at", pa.timestamp("us", tz="UTC"), nullable=True),
158	            pa.field("expected_delivery", pa.date32(), nullable=True),
159	            pa.field("load_ts", pa.timestamp("us", tz="UTC"), nullable=False),
160	        ]
161	    )
162	
163	
164	def ensure_table(catalog: Any) -> Any:
165	    """Create namespace + table if absent, then return the loaded table."""
166	    catalog.create_namespace_if_not_exists(NAMESPACE)
167	    return catalog.create_table_if_not_exists(IDENTIFIER, schema=_iceberg_schema())
168	
169	
170	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
171	# Batch generation.
172	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
173	
174	
175	def build_batch(rng: Rng, now: dt.datetime, rows: int) -> Any:
176	    """Build one referentially-consistent pyarrow batch with seeded DQ issues.
177	
178	    ``now`` anchors ``load_ts`` (so a freshness monitor on ``load_ts`` sees a genuinely
179	    fresh newest snapshot) and namespaces ``po_id`` so ticks never collide.
180	    """
181	    import pyarrow as pa
182	
183	    suppliers = rng.id_pool("SUP", N_SUPPLIERS, width=4)
184	    products = rng.id_pool("SKU", N_PRODUCTS)
185	    token = now.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")
186	
187	    po_id: list[str] = []
188	    po_line: list[int] = []
189	    supplier_id: list[str | None] = []
190	    product_id: list[str] = []
191	    order_qty: list[int] = []
192	    unit_cost: list[float] = []
193	    currency: list[str] = []
194	    status: list[str] = []
195	    ordered_at: list[dt.datetime] = []
196	    expected_delivery: list[dt.date] = []
197	    load_ts: list[dt.datetime] = []
198	
199	    # `rows` is the target line-row count. PO headers fan out to 1-4 lines each; we
200	    # stop emitting headers once the target is reached, then trim to exactly `rows`
201	    # (so a tick lands ~200-500 rows, not headers).
202	    header = 0
203	    while len(po_id) < rows:
204	        header += 1
205	        pid = f"PO-{token}-{header:05d}"
206	        placed = now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, 30), hours=rng.randint(0, 23))
207	        eta = (placed + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(3, 21))).date()
208	        # 1-4 lines per PO header (fan-out), one row per (po_id, po_line).
209	        for line in range(1, rng.randint(1, 4) + 1):
210	            sup: str | None = rng.choice(suppliers)
211	            qty = rng.randint(1, 500)
212	            # Seeded DQ issues (deterministic via rng draws):
213	            if rng.chance(NULL_SUPPLIER_RATE):
214	                sup = None  # -> fails not_null supplier_id
215	            if rng.chance(NEG_QTY_RATE):
216	                qty = -qty  # -> fails order_qty >= 0
217	            po_id.append(pid)
218	            po_line.append(line)
219	            supplier_id.append(sup)
220	            product_id.append(rng.choice(products))
221	            order_qty.append(qty)
222	            unit_cost.append(rng.money(1.5, 950.0))
223	            currency.append(rng.choice(CURRENCIES))
224	            status.append(rng.choice(PO_STATUSES))
225	            ordered_at.append(placed.replace(tzinfo=dt.UTC))
226	            expected_delivery.append(eta)
227	            load_ts.append(now)
228	
229	    # Trim the last header's overshoot so the batch is exactly `rows` line-rows.
230	    cols = [
231	        po_id,
232	        po_line,
233	        supplier_id,
234	        product_id,
235	        order_qty,
236	        unit_cost,
237	        currency,
238	        status,
239	        ordered_at,
240	        expected_delivery,
241	        load_ts,
242	    ]
243	    for col in cols:
244	        del col[rows:]
245	
246	    # Rare deliberate duplicate: copy a handful of whole rows -> (po_id, po_line) dupes.
247	    n = len(po_id)
248	    dup_count = max(1, int(n * DUP_RATE)) if n else 0
249	    for _ in range(dup_count):
250	        j = rng.randint(0, n - 1)
251	        po_id.append(po_id[j])
252	        po_line.append(po_line[j])
253	        supplier_id.append(supplier_id[j])
254	        product_id.append(product_id[j])
255	        order_qty.append(order_qty[j])
256	        unit_cost.append(unit_cost[j])
257	        currency.append(currency[j])
258	        status.append(status[j])

"""Flow D — Apache Iceberg writer (no orchestrator).

Each ``iceberg-tick`` appends a referentially-consistent batch of purchase-order
rows to the Iceberg table ``retail.purchase_orders`` via a pyiceberg **SqlCatalog**
(Postgres-backed metadata) with an **ADLS (abfss) warehouse** read through
fsspec/adlfs. DataQ reads the same table **natively** (its ``iceberg`` connection,
ADR 0030) on its own DataQ schedule — there is **no orchestrator and no
trigger-binding** (the Flow-C precedent: nothing "loads" this for DataQ to react to).

Self-contained by design — unlike the ``tick`` feeds this needs **no persisted
state file**. Each tick simply appends another snapshot (idempotent-safe: re-running
just adds another batch). ``po_id`` is namespaced by the tick's wall-clock so two
ticks never collide (which would forge an *accidental* duplicate and muddy the one
*deliberate* duplicate we seed). Supplier / product ids come from the same seeded
pools idiom (``rng.id_pool``) the rest of the harness uses, so they read as the same
id space as Flow A's ``suppliers`` / ``products``.

Seeded DQ issues per tick (mirrors ``dq_issues.py`` rates/style) give DataQ's checks
something real to bite on: ~1-2% negative ``order_qty`` (fails a ``order_qty >= 0``
range check), ~1% null ``supplier_id`` (fails ``not_null supplier_id``), and a rare
duplicate ``(po_id, po_line)`` (fails a uniqueness check).

The pyiceberg / pyarrow imports are module-local to the functions that need a live
catalog so ``python -m mockdata --help`` (and the other subcommands) don't pay for
them; ``iceberg-tick`` is the only path that requires the Iceberg deps.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import os
from typing import Any

from .rng import Rng

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Table coordinates + generation shape.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NAMESPACE = "retail"
TABLE = "purchase_orders"
IDENTIFIER = f"{NAMESPACE}.{TABLE}"

# Referential pools (same id shapes as Flow A: SUP-#### width 4, SKU-###### width 6).
N_SUPPLIERS = 30
N_PRODUCTS = 200

# Batch sizing + issue rates (mirror dq_issues.py: low single-digit %).
DEFAULT_ROWS_MIN = 200
DEFAULT_ROWS_MAX = 500
NEG_QTY_RATE = 0.015  # ~1.5% negative order_qty
NULL_SUPPLIER_RATE = 0.01  # ~1% null supplier_id
DUP_RATE = 0.005  # ~0.5% duplicated (po_id, po_line) rows

PO_STATUSES = ["open", "partial", "received", "cancelled"]
CURRENCIES = ["USD", "EUR", "GBP", "CAD", "JPY"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Catalog wiring.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def catalog_properties_from_env() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Compose ``load_catalog`` / ``SqlCatalog`` properties from the Job's env.

    ``ICEBERG_CATALOG_URI`` (the Postgres SQLAlchemy DSN, secret) + ``ICEBERG_WAREHOUSE``
    (the ``abfss://iceberg@<acct>.dfs.core.windows.net/warehouse`` root) + the ADLS
    account name/key for the fsspec (adlfs) FileIO. Mirrors the DataQ ``iceberg``
    connection's own catalog properties (``IcebergConfig.catalog_properties``) so both
    sides read the same table the same way.
    """
    uri = os.environ["ICEBERG_CATALOG_URI"]
    warehouse = os.environ["ICEBERG_WAREHOUSE"]
    props: dict[str, str] = {
        "uri": uri,
        "warehouse": warehouse,
        # Native (no query engine) object-store IO through fsspec/adlfs.
        "py-io-impl": "pyiceberg.io.fsspec.FsspecFileIO",
    }
    account = os.environ.get("AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME")
    key = os.environ.get("AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_KEY")
    if account:
        props["adls.account-name"] = account
    if key:
        props["adls.account-key"] = key
    return props


def build_catalog(
    name: str = "harness", *, properties: dict[str, str] | None = None
) -> Any:
    """Load a pyiceberg ``SqlCatalog`` (env-driven by default).

    ``properties`` overrides the env composition — the local sqlite smoke passes a
    ``sqlite://`` uri + a ``file://`` warehouse so the writer's real code paths run
    with no Azure. pyiceberg is imported here so the CLI stays import-cheap.
    """
    from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog

    props = properties if properties is not None else catalog_properties_from_env()
    return SqlCatalog(name, **props)


def _iceberg_schema() -> Any:
    """The ``retail.purchase_orders`` Iceberg schema (v2).

    ``po_id`` / ``po_line`` / ``load_ts`` are required (the batch always populates
    them); everything else is **optional** so the seeded null ``supplier_id`` lands
    instead of being rejected at write time. ``unit_cost`` is a ``double`` — it
    round-trips through pyarrow cleanly, avoiding decimal128 scale/precision friction
    on ``table.append`` (the design's allowed choice).
    """
    from pyiceberg.schema import Schema
    from pyiceberg.types import (
        DateType,
        DoubleType,
        IntegerType,
        NestedField,
        StringType,
        TimestamptzType,
    )

    return Schema(
        NestedField(1, "po_id", StringType(), required=True),
        NestedField(2, "po_line", IntegerType(), required=True),
        NestedField(3, "supplier_id", StringType(), required=False),
        NestedField(4, "product_id", StringType(), required=False),
        NestedField(5, "order_qty", IntegerType(), required=False),
        NestedField(6, "unit_cost", DoubleType(), required=False),
        NestedField(7, "currency", StringType(), required=False),
        NestedField(8, "status", StringType(), required=False),
        NestedField(9, "ordered_at", TimestamptzType(), required=False),
        NestedField(10, "expected_delivery", DateType(), required=False),
        NestedField(11, "load_ts", TimestamptzType(), required=True),
    )


def _arrow_schema() -> Any:
    """pyarrow schema matching ``_iceberg_schema`` (nullability + widths aligned).

    IntegerType → int32; TimestamptzType → ``timestamp('us', tz='UTC')`` (pyiceberg's
    required microsecond precision); DateType → date32. Nullable flags mirror the
    Iceberg ``required`` flags so ``table.append`` accepts the frame."""
    import pyarrow as pa

    return pa.schema(
        [
            pa.field("po_id", pa.string(), nullable=False),
            pa.field("po_line", pa.int32(), nullable=False),
            pa.field("supplier_id", pa.string(), nullable=True),
            pa.field("product_id", pa.string(), nullable=True),
            pa.field("order_qty", pa.int32(), nullable=True),
            pa.field("unit_cost", pa.float64(), nullable=True),
            pa.field("currency", pa.string(), nullable=True),
            pa.field("status", pa.string(), nullable=True),
            pa.field("ordered_at", pa.timestamp("us", tz="UTC"), nullable=True),
            pa.field("expected_delivery", pa.date32(), nullable=True),
            pa.field("load_ts", pa.timestamp("us", tz="UTC"), nullable=False),
        ]
    )


def ensure_table(catalog: Any) -> Any:
    """Create namespace + table if absent, then return the loaded table."""
    catalog.create_namespace_if_not_exists(NAMESPACE)
    return catalog.create_table_if_not_exists(IDENTIFIER, schema=_iceberg_schema())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Batch generation.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_batch(rng: Rng, now: dt.datetime, rows: int) -> Any:
    """Build one referentially-consistent pyarrow batch with seeded DQ issues.

    ``now`` anchors ``load_ts`` (so a freshness monitor on ``load_ts`` sees a genuinely
    fresh newest snapshot) and namespaces ``po_id`` so ticks never collide.
    """
    import pyarrow as pa

    suppliers = rng.id_pool("SUP", N_SUPPLIERS, width=4)
    products = rng.id_pool("SKU", N_PRODUCTS)
    token = now.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")

    po_id: list[str] = []
    po_line: list[int] = []
    supplier_id: list[str | None] = []
    product_id: list[str] = []
    order_qty: list[int] = []
    unit_cost: list[float] = []
    currency: list[str] = []
    status: list[str] = []
    ordered_at: list[dt.datetime] = []
    expected_delivery: list[dt.date] = []
    load_ts: list[dt.datetime] = []

    # `rows` is the target line-row count. PO headers fan out to 1-4 lines each; we
    # stop emitting headers once the target is reached, then trim to exactly `rows`
    # (so a tick lands ~200-500 rows, not headers).
    header = 0
    while len(po_id) < rows:
        header += 1
        pid = f"PO-{token}-{header:05d}"
        placed = now - dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, 30), hours=rng.randint(0, 23))
        eta = (placed + dt.timedelta(days=rng.randint(3, 21))).date()
        # 1-4 lines per PO header (fan-out), one row per (po_id, po_line).
        for line in range(1, rng.randint(1, 4) + 1):
            sup: str | None = rng.choice(suppliers)
            qty = rng.randint(1, 500)
            # Seeded DQ issues (deterministic via rng draws):
            if rng.chance(NULL_SUPPLIER_RATE):
                sup = None  # -> fails not_null supplier_id
            if rng.chance(NEG_QTY_RATE):
                qty = -qty  # -> fails order_qty >= 0
            po_id.append(pid)
            po_line.append(line)
            supplier_id.append(sup)
            product_id.append(rng.choice(products))
            order_qty.append(qty)
            unit_cost.append(rng.money(1.5, 950.0))
            currency.append(rng.choice(CURRENCIES))
            status.append(rng.choice(PO_STATUSES))
            ordered_at.append(placed.replace(tzinfo=dt.UTC))
            expected_delivery.append(eta)
            load_ts.append(now)

    # Trim the last header's overshoot so the batch is exactly `rows` line-rows.
    cols = [
        po_id,
        po_line,
        supplier_id,
        product_id,
        order_qty,
        unit_cost,
        currency,
        status,
        ordered_at,
        expected_delivery,
        load_ts,
    ]
    for col in cols:
        del col[rows:]

    # Rare deliberate duplicate: copy a handful of whole rows -> (po_id, po_line) dupes.
    n = len(po_id)
    dup_count = max(1, int(n * DUP_RATE)) if n else 0
    for _ in range(dup_count):
        j = rng.randint(0, n - 1)
        po_id.append(po_id[j])
        po_line.append(po_line[j])
        supplier_id.append(supplier_id[j])
        product_id.append(product_id[j])
        order_qty.append(order_qty[j])
        unit_cost.append(unit_cost[j])
        currency.append(currency[j])
        status.append(status[j])
        ordered_at.append(ordered_at[j])
        expected_delivery.append(expected_delivery[j])
        load_ts.append(load_ts[j])

    return pa.table(
        {
            "po_id": po_id,
            "po_line": po_line,
            "supplier_id": supplier_id,
            "product_id": product_id,
            "order_qty": order_qty,
            "unit_cost": unit_cost,
            "currency": currency,
            "status": status,
            "ordered_at": ordered_at,
            "expected_delivery": expected_delivery,
            "load_ts": load_ts,
        },
        schema=_arrow_schema(),
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tick entry point.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def run_tick(
    *,
    catalog: Any = None,
    properties: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    seed: int = 42,
    rows: int | None = None,
    now: dt.datetime | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Append one batch to ``retail.purchase_orders``; return commit stats.

    ``catalog`` (pre-built, used by the local smoke) takes precedence; otherwise a
    catalog is built from ``properties`` or the env. ``rows=None`` picks a seeded
    size in ``[DEFAULT_ROWS_MIN, DEFAULT_ROWS_MAX]``.
    """
    now = now or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC)
    # Per-tick seed shift so successive ticks differ yet stay reproducible.
    tick_token = int(now.timestamp())
    rng = Rng(seed + tick_token)
    if rows is None:
        rows = rng.randint(DEFAULT_ROWS_MIN, DEFAULT_ROWS_MAX)

    cat = catalog if catalog is not None else build_catalog(properties=properties)
    table = ensure_table(cat)
    batch = build_batch(rng, now, rows)
    table.append(batch)

    table.refresh()
    snapshot = table.current_snapshot()
    snapshot_id = snapshot.snapshot_id if snapshot is not None else None
    total_rows = int(table.scan().count())

    print(
        f"iceberg-tick {IDENTIFIER}: appended {batch.num_rows} rows "
        f"snapshot_id={snapshot_id} total_table_rows={total_rows}"
    )
    return {
        "identifier": IDENTIFIER,
        "appended_rows": batch.num_rows,
        "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
        "total_table_rows": total_rows,
    }

# DataQ re-provisioning — suite/check spec (authored via UI ONLY)

Applies to BOTH environments unless marked. Author through the real check editor
(catalog-driven column pickers, dry-run preview) — never the API or DB.
Where a column name below doesn't exist, pick the closest real column from the
editor's catalog/profiler and note the substitution in your report. Use dry-run
preview before saving each check where the editor offers it.

Dimension: accept the derived default; only set it manually where noted
(anomaly derives NULL by design — leave it unclassified).

## Suite 1 — "Snowflake — Orders (all paths)"
- Connection: "Snowflake — Retail" (both envs; live warehouse)
- Target: RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER
- Checks (9 — every kind Snowflake supports):
  1. `order_id not null` — expectation expect_column_values_to_not_be_null on the PK-ish id column.
  2. `order_id unique` — expectation expect_column_values_to_be_unique, same column.
  3. `status in allowed set` — expectation values_in_set on the status-like column; take the value list from the profiler/top-values so it passes.
  4. `no negative totals (custom SQL)` — custom SQL, rows returned = failures:
     `SELECT * FROM RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER WHERE <total/amount column> < 0`
  5. `orders freshness` — freshness kind on ORDER_TS; warn 336h, fail 720h.
  6. `orders volume` — volume kind; min 1000, max 10000000.
  7. `orders row-count anomaly` — anomaly kind, metric row_count, defaults
     (expect `skip` until baseline accrues — that is correct behavior).
  8. `orders schema drift` — schema_drift kind, capture baseline at creation.
  9. `orders reconcile vs Orders conn` — comparison kind; baseline connection
     "Snowflake — Orders", same table RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER, key = the id column,
     compare 2-3 value columns. Same physical table ⇒ should pass clean.

## Suite 2 — "Unity Catalog — Feedback (all paths)"
- Connection: "Unity Catalog — dataq_retail" (both envs; live warehouse)
- Target: dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment (~180 rows)
- Checks (9, mirror Suite 1's shapes):
  1. id/feedback key not-null; 2. same column unique (skip if visibly non-unique in profiler — use a compound/unique-looking column instead and note it);
  3. sentiment label in-set (values from profiler);
  4. custom SQL: rows where the sentiment score is outside its sane range (adapt to real column, e.g. `score NOT BETWEEN -1 AND 1`);
  5. freshness on scored_at — warn 336h fail 720h;
  6. volume min 50 max 1000000;
  7. anomaly row_count (defaults);
  8. schema drift (baseline now);
  9. comparison vs baseline connection "Unity Catalog — QA", same table, key = id column. Should pass clean.

## Suite 3 — "Iceberg — Purchase Orders"
- Connection: PROD = "harness-iceberg"; LOCAL = NEW connection "Iceberg — MinIO (local)" (recipe from the seeding agent's report; sql catalog @ postgres/iceberg_catalog, warehouse s3://iceberg/warehouse, MinIO endpoint, secret=s3.secret-access-key, catalog password = local dev pg password).
- Target: retail.purchase_orders
- Checks (6 — every kind Iceberg supports; no custom SQL / no anomaly by design):
  1. `po_id not null` — expectation.
  2. `supplier_id not null` — expectation. NOTE: ~1% seeded nulls ⇒ EXPECTED to warn/fail sometimes; that is deliberate (checks must bite). Set severity thresholds if the editor offers them: warn at >0%, fail at >5% unexpected.
  3. `order_qty >= 0` — expectation between min 0 (seeded ~1.5% negatives ⇒ same deal as above).
  4. `po freshness` — freshness on load_ts; warn 336h fail 720h.
  5. `po volume` — volume min 100.
  6. `po schema drift` — schema_drift, baseline now.
- Comparison deliberately omitted: no second connection holds this dataset; the comparison path is exercised by Suites 1/2/4. Note this in the report.

## Suite 4 — "Flat File — Logistics Tracking"
- Connection: PROD = "ADLS — landing (flat files)"; LOCAL = NEW connection "MinIO — landing (local)" (type s3, bucket landing, region us-east-1, endpoint_url http://minio:9000, addressing auto, access key = MINIO_ROOT_USER, secret = MinIO root password).
- Target: batch — prefix `adls_flatfile/logistics_tracking/`, pattern `tracking_events_([a-z_]+)\.csv`, strategy latest (PROD; this recreates the prior suite's proven target). LOCAL: find the equivalent tracking/logistics dataset path in the `landing` bucket (browse via the connection editor/profiler or the seeding layout) and use its real prefix/pattern; note what you used.
- Checks (6 — every kind flat files support; no custom SQL / no anomaly by design):
  1. `tracking_number not null` — expectation (adapt column name).
  2. `status in allowed set` — expectation, values from profiler.
  3. `event freshness (column)` — freshness on the event timestamp column; warn 336h fail 720h.
  4. `file arrival freshness` — freshness with NO column (arrival-time mode — the case a warehouse can't express); warn 336h fail 1440h.
  5. `tracking volume` — volume min 50.
  6. `tracking schema drift` — schema_drift, baseline now.

## Phase 3 — orchestration (after all suites exist in the env)
- Trigger bindings (provider = airflow):
  - PROD (connection "Apache Airflow (dev)" / env dev): `flow_a_snowflake_load` → Suite 1; `flow_b_medallion` → Suite 2.
  - LOCAL (NEW connection "Airflow — local", base_url http://airflow-webserver:8080, basic auth admin + password from DataQ-harness/local/.env): same two bindings.
  - Iceberg + flat-file suites get NO binding (no DAG feeds them) — schedules only.
- Schedules (all 4 suites, both envs): daily crons, staggered — Suite 1 `0 5 * * *`, Suite 2 `15 5 * * *`, Suite 3 `30 5 * * *`, Suite 4 `45 5 * * *`, enabled.

## Verification (Phase 4a)
- Run each suite once from the UI (Run now), watch live progress, record per-check outcomes. Expected: mostly pass; anomaly checks `skip` (cold start); Iceberg supplier_id/order_qty checks may warn/fail on seeded issues (EXPECTED); everything else green. Any operational `error` status = real defect, report it.

Worth flagging upstream in the harness — `iceberg_writer.py`'s docstring assumes wall-clock separation that isn't guaranteed for rapid successive calls.

s3.path-style-access: true          (required — MinIO serves the bucket in the path, not virtual-host)

**Important gotcha for the recipe:** pyiceberg's `SqlCatalog` scopes tables by the catalog **name** (the first positional arg to `SqlCatalog(...)` / `load_catalog(...)`), not just the DB. Connection: Snowflake — Retail (DATAQ_READER) (closest match to spec's "Snowflake — Retail"). Target: `RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER`. 9 checks, all dry-run-verified before saving:
1. `order_number not null` (expect_column_values_to_not_be_null) — **substitution**: no `order_id` column exists; catalog only has `order_number` (string, e.g. `ORD-00000001`). Pass.

3. `status in allowed set` — values from profiler: `delivered, shipped, placed, returned, cancelled`. Pass.
4. `no negative totals (custom SQL)` — `SELECT * FROM {batch} WHERE order_total < 0`. Pass, 0 rows.

### Suite 2 — "Unity Catalog — Feedback (all paths)"
Connection: Unity Catalog — dataq_retail. Target: `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment`. 8 checks (custom SQL skipped — see defect below):
1. `feedback_id not null`. Pass. (feedback_id is the real id column; profiler confirmed 180 rows / 180 distinct, genuinely unique, so no substitution needed for uniqueness either.)

5. `tracking volume`, min 50 / max 1,000,000 (spec only gave a min; UI requires both min and max, so I added a generous max).

I did a read-only S3 listing (boto3, verification-only) and found the real local prefix/files mirror PROD exactly: `adls_flatfile/logistics_tracking/tracking_events_{delivered,in_transit,ready}.csv`. Since `strategy=latest` picks the lexicographically-greatest capture-group value ("ready" > "in_transit" > "delivered"), I set the literal `target_path` to `adls_flatfile/logistics_tracking/tracking_events_ready.csv` to match what batch resolution would have picked.

The check category picker doesn't gate "Custom SQL" by datasource capability, so a UC suite can start building a check that can never pass.
2. **Flat-file batch targets (prefix + pattern + strategy) have no UI.** Fully implemented backend capability with zero corresponding form fields; only a literal single-file path is settable through the UI.
3. **Iceberg connections with non-default catalog properties (`catalog_name`, `properties` dict, second `catalog_secret_name`) have no UI.** Confirmed via a failed Test Connection attempt; these fields are backend-only ("API-settable" per the frontend's own source comment).

Issue 1 — title: "Custom SQL check unusable on Unity Catalog suites: dry-run fails with 'No provider found for unexpected_rows_query.table using PandasExecutionEngine'"
Body: On a Unity Catalog suite (target dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment), authoring a Custom SQL check and hitting dry-run always errors with `No provider found for unexpected_rows_query.table using PandasExecutionEngine`. Reproduced with two different SQL bodies including a trivial `WHERE 1=0`, so it is an engine-compatibility gap, not a query bug: the UC runner reads the table into a pandas-backed GX DataFrame asset (`backend/app/datasources/unity_catalog.py`), and GX's `unexpected_rows_query` expectation requires a SQL execution engine. docs/feature-matrix.md marks Custom SQL ✅ for Unity Catalog — so either this is a regression or the ✅ never actually worked through this path (the #953 "matrix tick that never ran live" shape — needs a live check of whether any UC custom-SQL check has ever produced a non-error result). Also: the check-editor category picker does not gate Custom SQL by datasource capability, so users can author a check that can never run. Acceptance: either make custom SQL work on UC (SQL-side execution) or gate it out of the UC check editor AND correct the feature matrix.

Issue 2 — title: "Suite target UI has no batch fields (prefix/pattern/strategy) — backend flat-file batch resolution unreachable from the UI"
Body: The backend fully supports batch targets for flat-file suites (`resolve_batch`/`BatchSpec` in backend/app/datasources/registry.py + flatfile.py; prod's former "Logistics Tracking — flat file" suite used prefix `adls_flatfile/logistics_tracking/` + pattern `tracking_events_([a-z_]+)\.csv` + strategy latest). But `frontend/src/components/suites/SuiteForm.tsx` exposes only a literal single `target_path` — there is no way to author or edit a batch target through the UI. Found while recreating the logistics suite via UI: had to fall back to the literal file `.../tracking_events_ready.csv` that strategy=latest would have picked. Acceptance: suite form supports prefix/pattern/strategy batch targets (with the same preview the backend batch resolution gives).

Issue 3 — title: "Iceberg connection editor lacks catalog_name, properties dict, and catalog_secret_name — non-default catalogs cannot be configured via UI"
Body: `IcebergConfig` (backend/app/datasources/iceberg.py) supports `catalog_name`, arbitrary catalog/storage `properties`, and a second credential via `catalog_secret_name` (the sql-catalog DB password). The connection editor (`frontend/src/components/connections/connectionFormSpec.ts`) exposes only catalog_type/catalog_uri/warehouse/secret_property + ONE secret slot — its own comment marks the rest "advanced (API-settable)". Concrete consequence found live: an Iceberg table on an S3-compatible warehouse (MinIO; sql catalog on Postgres) is fully readable by the backend (verified in-worker with pyiceberg PyArrowFileIO + s3.endpoint + s3.path-style-access + catalog_name), but the connection is impossible to create through the UI — Test Connection can never pass because the catalog DB password has no field, and a non-default catalog_name (required: SqlCatalog scopes tables by catalog NAME; a mismatch raises NoSuchTableError) cannot be set. Acceptance: editor exposes catalog_name, a key/value properties editor, and the second catalog credential.

Issue 4 — title: "PII-column heuristic pre-fills obviously non-PII columns (rating, sentiment, carrier, location_city)"
Body: While authoring suites via UI, the auto-populated "PII columns" panel pre-selected `rating` + `sentiment` (dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment) and `carrier` + `location_city` (logistics tracking CSV) as PII without user input. Ratings, sentiment labels, carrier names and city names (absent any person link) are not personal data in these schemas; over-flagging dilutes the redaction signal and trains users to ignore the panel. Review the heuristic's term list/matching (likely substring matches on generic words). Low priority.

Report: for each issue — filed number + labels + milestone, or the duplicate you commented on instead. Verify each created issue with `gh issue view <n> --json labels,milestone,title` per repo hygiene.
